# Provital platform

Engineering workspace for the Provital platform build. The documents in [`docs/`](docs/) are the proposed architecture, infrastructure and the delivery plan to launch.

| Document | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) | Target architecture: runtime units, modules, data, key flows and the rules CI checks |
| [Infrastructure](docs/infrastructure.md) | What the platform needs to run, the target topology, environments and cloud options |
| [Delivery plan](docs/delivery-plan.md) | Milestones to launch: team, two-week sprints, Jira tracking and the UAT, RC and launch checklists |
| [Discovery baseline](docs/discovery-baseline.md) | Engineering digest of the Discovery package v0.1, with the item IDs |

## Status

| | |
|---|---|
| Phase | Setup, week 0 |
| Date | 2 November 2026 |
| Source | Discovery package v0.1, `57blocks/provital-discovery`, `outputs/discovery/`, commit `733e97e` |
| Tracking | Jira project `AN`, [board 1144](https://57blocks.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/AN/boards/1144/backlog) |
| Decisions | ADRs 0002 to 0014 are under review. The `docs/adr/` index is still to be added |

The documents are proposals. They become the baseline when the ADRs they cite are accepted.

## Repository conventions

- Trunk-based development on `main`. Short-lived branches, squash merge, one review at least (see [delivery plan section 8](docs/delivery-plan.md#8-ways-of-working)).
- Conventional Commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`.
- A change to a module boundary, a contract, the data model or the technology needs an ADR first.

## 5. Integration facts (T2)

- **One interface design for both ERPs** (T2-D-001). NAV receives the part of the payload it can use.
- **No direct database access** (T2-D-002). The order hand-off starts on NAV's file import.
- **Every outbound message** is stored until the ERP confirms it (T2-D-005), carries a business key (T2-D-006), and is reconciled daily by count and total (T2-D-007).
- **One authenticated, encrypted connection** to the ERP. Every message is logged with personal data masked (T2-D-008).
- **Order number ranges** of the platform and the current shop cannot collide. NAV replaces an order with the same number, so a resend runs a pre-check first (T2-O-002).
- **The acceptance signal** is the order status read. The outbox keeps the order until it appears (T2-O-003).
- **Synchronous calls** exist only for the payment provider, the address validation, and the reads of payment options, vouchers (fallback) and order history (T2 section 4). Everything else is asynchronous.
- **Flows:** 9 outbound (T2-C-001 to -009), 15 inbound (T2-C-010 to -024), 8 external systems (T2-C-030 to -037).
- **NAV changes N-1 to N-12** each have a fallback (T2 section 3). The build must contain the fallbacks. A fallback still in use three months after R1 becomes a platform function through change control.

**Maximum age of a copy at the checkout** (T2 section 5):

| Copy | Maximum age | If older |
|---|---|---|
| Articles and stock | 1 hour | Sell; mark the availability as not current; record the version |
| Prices, campaigns | 1 hour | Sell at the last prices; the order records their version |
| Shipping fees | 1 day | The last fee set applies; the order records its version |
| Vouchers | 5 minutes, plus a live read | A voucher that cannot be confirmed is not accepted |
| Customer, assignment, payment options | 1 day | Payment options: only card and PayPal. Others: the last copy; the order records its age |

**During an ERP outage** the shop sells from the copies, and orders wait in the outbox. The outbox drains in order when the ERP returns.

**What we know about NAV today** (internal analysis, `internals/analyses/NAV_Order_Flat_File_Reconstructed_Example.md`): the current shop sends an order as a text file with one `KEY<TAB>value` pair per line, German decimal commas, through the NAV SOAP function `ProvideOrderData`. Several value lists and formats are still unknown. The contract (T2-AC-001) must close these gaps.

# ADR-0015 Advisor master data read through the ERP port

| | |
|---|---|
| Status | Proposed |
| Date | 5 November 2026 |
| Deciders | Tech lead |
| Related | ADR-0004 (the ERP port), T3-D-005, T2-D-009 |

## Context

Head office needs the advisor master data that the ERP holds: advisor number (`B` and five digits), given name, family name, e-mail address and the active flag. The ERP is the master of advisor data (DP1 section 3.1). The architecture gives the `identity` module the read of customer and advisor master data, through `integration` ([architecture section 4](../architecture.md#4-modules)). The ERP port of ADR-0004 has one operation, `readCustomer`. A new operation on the port is a contract change and needs an ADR ([AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)).

## Decision

1. The ERP port gains the payload contract `AdvisorMasterData` and the operation `readAdvisor(advisorNumber)`. It returns `null` when the ERP has no advisor with this number. Every adapter implements it; the fake adapter seeds advisor `B20001` with synthetic data.
2. The `integration` module exposes `readAdvisor`. Like `readCustomer`, the result carries `source`, `sourceVersion` and `readAt` (T2-D-009).
3. The `identity` module exposes `getAdvisor(advisorNumber)`. It depends on the public API of `integration` and returns `{ advisorNumber, givenName, familyName, email, active, sourceVersion, readAt }` or `null`. The platform stores no advisor master data in the `identity` schema; this is a live read, not a copy.
4. An ERP outage surfaces as `ErpUnavailableError` to the caller. The caller decides the fallback.

## Consequences

- `identity` now depends on `integration`. The dependency runs one way; `integration` does not import `identity`, so rule 4 of the architecture (no module cycles) holds.
- The NAV adapter must implement `readAdvisor` before the gateway serves production reads. Until then the fake adapter answers.
- A read copy of advisor master data (T3-D-007), with the maximum age of T2 section 5, is a later decision. When it comes, `identity.getAdvisor` keeps its shape and reads the copy instead.
- The contract snapshot check of architecture section 9 shows the new payload when it exists.
